chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a slave owned among partners, and one of them emancipates his share. He said: 'That is a harm against his companions — they are not able to sell him nor to hire out his services.' He said: 'He (the slave) is appraised at a price, and it is then imposed upon the one who emancipated him as a punishment. And indeed it was only made (obligatory) upon him because of what he damaged.'

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوك: A slave or owned person; in jurisprudence, one in a state of legal ownership (milk) by another
key_terms.شُرَكَاء: Partners or co-owners sharing ownership of property, here a jointly-owned slave
key_terms.عُقُوبَة: Punishment or penalty; here a financial penalty as deterrence against unauthorized emancipation
key_terms.فَسَاد: Spoiling, harm, or corruption; the legal concept of causing damage or disruption to another's rights
key_terms.مُؤَاجَرَة: Hiring out (someone's) labor or services for payment; a recognized contract in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on emancipating a jointly-owned slave without the co-owners' consent?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules on the case where a jointly-owned slave is emancipated by one of the partners without the consent of the others. The Imam explains that this act constitutes harm to the remaining co-owners, as it leaves the slave in a legally ambiguous state — neither fully free nor able to be sold or hired out. As a remedy and punishment for causing this harm, the one who emancipated his share must pay the full appraised value of the slave to compensate his partners.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the slave owned between partners, so one of them emancipates his share. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is a spoiling (of matters) upon his companion not being able upon selling him, nor hiring out his services’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His price would be evaluated, so it would be made upon the one who emancipated him as a punishment. But rather, that is made to be upon him due to what he spoilt’.
